1.text:
The construction that is actually described is the one-point-per-axis
cross simplex.  Up to relabelling

${\cal C}_{d}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\},\qquad 
X_{k}=t_{k}e_{k},~t_{k}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1)$,

so that on the event which is the construction by definition

$$
V_{d}= {\rm Leb}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
     =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|}{d!}
     =\frac1{d!}\prod_{k=1}^{d}|t_{k}|\quad{\rm a.s.}
$$

and with $E|t|=1/2$

$$
EV_{d}= \frac{(E|t|)^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad EV_{1}=1/2 .
$$

For $i\ne j$, on the same axis

$$
E_{0}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      =0.7651957\ldots ,
$$

and $E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|t|=1/2$.  For the $d+1$ points 
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

$$
\bar d_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{0}}{d+1},\qquad \bar d_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence with the conventional normalisation

$$
R_{d}^{0}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar d_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{0}\bigr]},\qquad 
R_{1}^{0}=1,
$$

$R_{d}^{0}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}^{0}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}^{0}=3/[4(1+E_{0})]\approx0.212441$,
* $R_{3}^{0}\approx0.032933$,
* $R_{4}^{0}\approx0.003951$,
* $R_{5}^{0}\approx0.000385$,
* $R_{6}^{0}\approx3.2\times10^{-5}$,

the tail being $<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge7$.  Thus

$$
S_{0}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}
   =1+0.212441+0.032933+0.003951+0.000385+\cdots
   =1.2497\ldots\approx1.250
$$

to three decimals, $1+R_{2}^{0}=1.2124$ already giving the bulk of the
mass.  In $E_{0}$-free normalisation this is $\sum_{d}2^{-d}/d!E_{0}
=(e^{1/2}-1)/E_{0}\approx0.848$.

The $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor $EV_{d}^{\rm iid}=2^{-d}/d^{d}$ and the
corresponding sum $\sum R_{d}^{\rm iid}\approx1.1172\approx1.117$ is
the i.i.d. draw $X_{i}=U_{i}e_{J_{i}}$ from the whole union.  It is the
correct value under a literal union-i.i.d. sampling interpretation, but
it is obtained precisely by discarding the textual requirement
“distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ with
$|\{points\}|=|\{segments\}|=d$, i.e. by allowing axis collisions.
With the bijective one-point-per-axis reading forced by the wording the
collision loss is identically $1$ and the distinct-axis sum $1.250$ is
the one consistent with the stated geometry.

2.text:
The cross

$${\cal C}_{n}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{n}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}, \qquad 
X_{k}=t_{k}e_{k},\;t_{k}\sim U(-1,1) \;{\rm i.i.d.},$$

is the direct reading of “distinct mutually orthogonal open line
segments’’ with $|\{X_{k}\}|=|\{ {\rm segments}\}|=n$, up to relabelling.
On the event which is the construction

$$
V_{n}={\rm Leb}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\right)
      =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{n}]|}{n!}
      =\frac1{n!}\prod_{k=1}^{n}|t_{k}|\qquad{\rm a.s.}
$$

so that with $E|t|=1/2$

$$
EV_{n}= \frac{(E|t|)^{n}}{n!}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},\qquad EV_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Put

$$
E_{0}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     \approx0.7651957,
$$

and $E\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$.  For the $n+1$ points
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

$$
\bar d_{n}

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The explicit wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” whose number equals the ambient dimension forces a fixed orthogonal frame with exactly one uniform coordinate per axis. This geometry yields the determinant identity without any combinatorial prefactor, so EV_d = 2^{-d}/d! exactly. The mean pairwise distance then reduces to the closed expression [1+(d-1)E_0]/(d+1) with the already-computed constant E_0 ≈ 0.765196. The resulting series begins 1 + 0.212441 + 0.032933 + 0.003951 + … and reaches 1.2497 after only six terms; the super-exponential tail beyond d = 6 lies below 4 × 10^{-5}. Consequently the three-decimal sum is unambiguously 1.250, insensitive to truncation. Any appeal to the alternative 1.117 figure would require replacing the prescribed one-point-per-segment construction by an i.i.d. draw over the entire union—an interpretation that directly contradicts the “distinct” qualifier and re-introduces an extraneous d!/d^d collision factor never present in the stated geometry. The rapid decay likewise removes any residual concern about high-dimensional contributions, confirming that 1.250 is the unique stable three-decimal value consistent with the problem statement.

6.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The explicit requirement of distinct mutually orthogonal segments, with cardinality exactly matching dimension, fixes a deterministic axis assignment that eliminates any combinatorial prefactor. Consequently the volume expectation collapses cleanly to 2^{-d}/d! while the mean pairwise distance remains the closed elementary expression [1+(d-1)E_0]/(d+1). Summing the resulting series through d=8 already yields 1.24971 with an analytically bounded tail smaller than 3\times10^{-6}; three-decimal rounding is therefore insensitive to truncation and stabilizes unambiguously at 1.250. Any model that inserts a d!/d^d collision term would require reinterpreting the segments as exchangeable rather than prescribed, directly contradicting the wording. The numerical stability of the first four terms (already >1.249) together with the super-exponential decay therefore confirms that 1.250 is the unique value consistent with the stated geometry.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 4, 6 and 7 have rightly stressed the rapid convergence and the super-exponential tail bound, both of which are indisputable once the expectations are written down. Yet the decisive textual hinge remains whether “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments” with matching cardinalities compels a fixed, bijective assignment or merely requires that the realized segments be pairwise orthogonal after sampling. If the latter reading is admissible, the natural generative model reverts to independent uniform draws over the entire union; each new point then lands on an axis chosen uniformly from the d possibilities, restoring the combinatorial prefactor d!/d^d inside EV_d. The resulting series is then precisely the one that sums to 1.1172, already within 0.0003 of its three-decimal value after only four terms. Because the problem statement never explicitly forbids axis collisions—only that the supporting segments ultimately be distinct and orthogonal—the i.i.d.-over-union construction satisfies every literal constraint while remaining probabilistically well-defined for every finite d. In that light the 1.117 figure is not an extraneous alternative but the value obtained when the wording is interpreted in its weakest, purely geometric sense. Given the numerical stability already demonstrated for both series, a final ratification of 1.250 would therefore require an additional, stronger assumption (strict pre-assignment of axes) that the problem never states.

5.text:
The wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ with
$|\{X_{k}\}|=|\{{\rm segments}\}|=d$ fixes a bijection point$\leftrightarrow$axis.
Up to relabelling

${\cal C}_{d}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\},\qquad
X_{k}=t_{k}e_{k},\;t_{k}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}U(-1,1)$

and on the construction

$V_{d}={\rm Leb}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
      =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|}{d!}
      =\frac1{d!}\prod_{k=1}^{d}|t_{k}|\ {\rm a.s.}$

Hence with $E|t|=1/2$

$EV_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $\;EV_{1}=1/2$.

For $i\ne j$

$E_{0}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$,
$E\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$.

For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\}$ the mean unordered pair
distance is

$\bar d_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{0}}{d+1},\qquad \bar d_{1}=1/2$.

Hence in the conventional normalisation

$R_{d}^{0}:=\dfrac{EV_{d}}{\bar d_{d}}
   =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{0}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,$

$R_{d}^{0}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.

Numerically

$R_{1}^{0}=1.000000$,
$R_{2}^{0}=3/[4(1+E_{0})]\approx0.212441$,
$R_{3}^{0}\approx0.032933$,
$R_{4}^{0}\approx0.003951$,
$R_{5}^{0}\approx0.000385$,
$R_{6}^{0}\approx3.2\times10^{-5}$,

tail $<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge7$.

So

$S_{0}^{\rm dist}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}
 =1+0.212441+0.032933+0.003951+0.000385+\cdots
 =1.2497\ldots$

i.e. $1.250$ to three decimals.  $1+R_{2}=1.2124$ already gives the bulk
of the mass and the remainder after $d=6$ is $<4\times10^{-5}$.

This is the one-point-per-axis, distinct-segment reading forced by the
statement.  The $d!/d^{d}$ i.i.d. over the whole union alternative
$EV_{d}^{\rm iid}=2^{-d}/d^{d}$ gives $\sum R_{d}^{\rm iid}\approx1.1172$,
but it re-introduces axis collisions that are excluded by the
“distinct’’ qualifier.  With the prescribed geometry the stable three-
decimal sum is $1.250$.

Put 
${\cal C}_{d}=\cup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}$ and up to relabelling
$X_{k}=t_{k}e_{k}$, $t_{k}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1)$.

On $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$

$$
V_{d}= {\rm Leb}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}\bigr)
     =\frac{|\det[X_{1}\ldots X_{d}]|}{d!}
     =\frac1{d!}\prod_{k=1}^{d}|t_{k}|\;\;{\rm a.s.}
$$

Hence with $E|t|=1/2$

$$
EV_{d}= \frac{(E|t|)^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad EV_{1}=1/2,
$$

and no $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor is present because the $d$ segments
are distinct and $|\{X_{k}\}|=|\{ {\rm segments}\}|=d$ by construction.

$E\|0-X_{k}\|=1/2$ and for $i\ne j$ on the same axis

$$
E_{0}:=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
      =E\sqrt{t_{i}^{2}+t_{j}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      =0.7651957\ldots .
$$

For the $d+1$ points the mean unordered pair distance is

$$
\bar d_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{0}}{d+1},\qquad \bar d_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence with the conventional normalisation

$$
R_{d}^{0}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar d_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[\,1+(d-1)E_{0}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,
$$

   =1+0.212441+0.032933+0.003951+0.000385+\cdots
   =1.2497\ldots\approx1.250
$$

to three decimals.  $1+R_{2}=1.2124$ already carries the bulk of the mass
and the remainder after $d=6$ is $<4\times10^{-5}$.

In $E_{0}$-free normalisation $\sum_{d}2^{-d}/(d!E_{0})=(e^{1/2}-1)/E_{0}
\approx0.848$.
